headline: 3 burnt in suspected gas explosion at Kalabagan house
summary: Three young men were rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital after a blast occurred in a ground-floor room in Dhaka's Kalabagan area.
details: Three people suffered burn injuries in a suspected gas explosion at a house in Dhaka’s Kalabagan early today. The injured—Rana (22), Jewel (20), and Parvez (21)—were rushed to the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
The incident occurred around 12:00 am at a house on Box Culvert Road in the Free School Street area. Jewel lives in the house, and had invited his friends Rana and Parvez to stay over for the night.
According to doctors at the burn unit, Rana suffered burns to 63 percent of his body, while Jewel and Parvez suffered burns to 30 percent and 21 percent of their bodies respectively.
A furniture trader, Imran Hossain Rajib, reported that the house is a seven-storey building with a septic tank located directly beneath Jewel’s ground-floor room.
Rajib further claimed that the floor of the room was always unusually hot and that a smell of gas could often be detected while passing the building.
He added that Jewel’s family had repeatedly informed the landlord about these issues, but no action was taken to address the concerns.

headline: Air Quality: Dhaka ranks joint top in global air pollution index
summary: The capital city has reached the most polluted city in the world ranking on Thursday morning.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the most polluted city in the world, sharing the top spot in the global air pollution index on Thursday morning.
The city's air quality has deteriorated significantly, placing it at the joint top of the global rankings for pollution levels.
High levels of particulate matter and pollutants in the air make the city's air quality hazardous for residents and visitors alike.
This ranking highlights the ongoing struggle with air pollution in the capital, a recurring issue that affects public health and visibility.
